Colon: Structure, function, and disorders
193


Mucus secreted by colonic goblet cells forms a physical barrier to bacterial pathogens known as the unstirred layer, and is
routinely cleared by the colon. In CF, as with pulmonary secretions, colonic secretions are underhydrated, and this renders the
unstirred mucus layer thicker and less able to clear trapped bacteria, which is thought to contribute to colonic inﬂammation
frequently seen in this condition.
